milestones.name: ATC Flight Plan Activated
rules: The Airport CDM Platform checks consistency between ATC Flight Plan, Airport Slot and Airport flight data and then confirms the flight to the Network Operations and allows further local processing of the flight.
This check shall be performed to verify the consistency between the ATC Flight Plan, Airport Slot and Airport flight data before the first E-DPI is sent.

The AO must provide correct information before this first E-DPI message, in order to feed Network Operations with consistent SOBT, aircraft registration, and first destination data, as early in time as possible.
The E-DPI message should not be sent if no or inconsistent information is provided.
This process is triggered by the first activation of the ATC Flight Plan (earliest EOBT-3 hr), or by new or late submissions of the ATC Flight Plan, after cancellation or revised EOBT.
For an arrival, ELDT and EIBT are updated; for a departure, EOBT and ETOT are updated.
The DPI process commences the correct messaging with Network Operations (if implemented).
The flight is ready not later than 15 minutes after the planned EOBT.

milestones.name: EOBT - 2 hr
rules: The Network Operations issues the CTOT and sends it to relevant ATS units as well as the departure aerodrome.
If the flight is regulated, a CTOT is issued at EOBT-2h.
For inbound flights, ELDT is updated based on information provided by the FUM messages, taking into account the actual progress of the flight.

The process checks (before or after take off from outstation) whether AO/GH flight estimates are consistent with the ATC Flight Plan and informs Network Operations about the updated take off time estimate, using a T-DPI Message.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan estimated off block time at EOBT-2 hrs.
At EOBT-2 hrs Network Operations is informed through the first T-DPI message.
Calculation basis for the TTOT shall take into account EIBT+MTTT+EXOT, if later than EOBT+EXOT.
In the case of manual input of TOBT, this estimate will override the EIBT+MTTT estimate, hence TTOT equals TOBT+EXOT.
The Airport CDM Platform marks appropriate fields as REGULATED and updates ETOT/TTOT/CTOT.
other_concepts: priority of CTOT flights over unregulated flights

milestones.name: Take Off from Outstation
rules: The outstation provides ATOT to the Network Operations and Aircraft Operator.
The accuracy of ATOT is +/- 1 minute.
If the departure airport is more than 3hrs flying time from the destination airport the ATOT is received from either the Network Operations FUM or via the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler.
Using the ATOT an ELDT can be calculated by using the Estimated Elapsed Time on the FPL.

If the flight is within 3hrs flying time of the destination airport the Network Operations monitors progress of the flight using the ETFMS and sends a Flight Update Message (FUM) that provides updates of the flight's progress.

The process checks whether the AO/GH estimated landing time after take off from outstation are consistent with the outbound ATC Flight Plan, and when needed informs the Network Operations about the updated take off time estimates using a T-DPI-t Message.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan at take off from outstation.
A TTOT tolerance of 5 minutes is respected before Network Operations is informed of the updated TTOT.
Calculation basis for the TTOT shall take into account EIBT+MTTT+EXOT.
In case EOBT is later than EIBT+MTTT, TTOT equals EOBT+EXOT.
In the case where TOBT is available this prediction will overrule the EIBT+MTTT estimate, hence TTOT equals TOBT+EXOT.

milestones.name: Local Radar Update
rules: The radar system detects a flight based upon the assigned SSR code when the flight crosses a defined FIR/ATC boundary.
Update of the ELDT can trigger a new TOBT to be entered by the AO/GH, or calculated automatically by the Airport CDM Platform.
Taking into account the taxi-in time (EXIT), any change to a stand or gate is not preferred after ELDT-30'.
The update of TOBT for the related departing flight takes place following this milestone.
An estimated in-block time (EIBT) is computed using the ELDT and the estimated taxi-in time.
The process commences the TOBT process and checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT.
The TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed of updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by the detection of the flight by radar in either FIR, TMA, or on Final Approach.
other_concepts: objective to decrease stand and gate changes in last 30 minutes

milestones.name: Final Approach
rules: The radar system detects a flight based upon the assigned SSR code and identifies when the flight crosses either a defined range/position or passes/leaves a predetermined level.
Update of the ELDT is used to determine a new TOBT.
The process commences the TOBT process and checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT.
The TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed of updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by the detection of the flight by radar in either FIR, TMA, or on Final Approach.

milestones.name: Landed
rules: The occurrence of ALDT triggers an update of downstream estimates: TOBT and TTOT are updated automatically or inserted manually by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, calculated on the basis of the defined turn-round period for the departing flight.
The EIBT can be updated according to the ALDT+EXIT.
The process checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT or ATC Flight Plan.
A TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed on updated TTOT.

milestones.name: In-Block
rules: The occurrence of AIBT should trigger an update of downstream estimates: TOBT and TTOT are updated automatically or inserted manually by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, calculated on the basis of the estimated turn-round period for the departing flight.
The process checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT or ATC Flight Plan.
A TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed on updated TTOT.
other_concepts: ACGT is considered to commence at AIBT

milestones.name: Ground Handling Started
rules: The occurrence of ACGT triggers an update of downstream estimates: TOBT is updated automatically or inserted manually by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, calculated on the basis of the estimated turn-round period for the departing flight.
The process checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT or ATC Flight Plan.
A TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed on updated TTOT.

milestones.name: Final Confirmation of the TOBT
rules: The Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler provides their most accurate TOBT taking into account the operational situation, t minutes before EOBT (t is a parameter time agreed locally).

Following the receipt of the TOBT, the ATC system calculates and provides the Estimated Taxi-Out Time (EXOT) based on the predicted traffic load, gate/stand location, runway in use, and waiting period at the Holding Position, etc.
The flight is introduced into the pre-departure sequence.
The process checks whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This check should be performed at a predefined time (local parameter) to confirm TOBT prior to TSAT issue and verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan estimates given the updated TOBT.
A TTOT tolerance is respected before Network Operations is informed on updated TTOT.
This process is triggered by a new TOBT or TTOT update.
There is no need to confirm an existing TOBT if it has been manually modified before.

milestones.name: TSAT Issued
rules: ATC informs all relevant partners of the TSAT that has been allocated to the flight.
The Network Operations is informed by a T-DPI-s for non regulated flights.
The process checks whether the number of TOBT updates exceeds a tolerance defined locally, after TSAT has been issued.
The TSAT indicates to the partners the time when the start up approval can be expected.
A check shall be performed to see the number of TOBT updates after TSAT has been issued.
In case the number of TOBT updates exceeds a threshold, then the TOBT input should be processed according to local procedure.
This process is triggered by a defined time (local parameter) before TOBT, or by a TOBT update after TSAT issue.

milestones.name: Boarding Starts
rules: ASBT is provided automatically from the airport system or by manual input by Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler.
The process informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Start Boarding Time (ASBT) when it occurs.
The process checks whether boarding starts in time to respect TOBT and informs the AO/GH in case TOBT needs to be updated.
At a certain time before TOBT (local variable e.g. corresponding to aircraft type) a check shall be performed to check the boarding status.
This process is triggered by a time variable <value> minutes before TOBT.

milestones.name: Aircraft Ready
rules: The process informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Ready Time (ARDT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft is ready for start up/push-back.
The process informs the AO/GH that TOBT has passed and the Airport CDM Platform has not yet received ARDT or Ready Status (RDY).
At TOBT + tolerance the AO/GH are informed that TOBT has passed and there has not been a ready status message yet.
ATC refines the pre-departure sequence.
The pilot requests start up just before TSAT, following coordination with the Ground Handler.

milestones.name: Start Up Requested
rules: ATC confirms TSAT to the pilot in order to maintain the aircraft in the pre-departure sequence.
ATC assures that a regulated flight can respect its CTOT, provided the aircraft was ready on time (ARDT).
The process informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Start up Request Time (ASRT) in the Airport CDM Platform when it occurs.
The process alerts all relevant Airport CDM Partners when no start up has been requested inside the locally agreed TSAT tolerance window.
If the start up request is not made by TSAT + tolerance, the AO/GH is informed that no start up has been requested, and should update TOBT.

milestones.name: Start Up Approved
rules: The process informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual start up approval Time (ASAT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft has received start up approval/push-back clearance when it occurs.
The process checks if ASAT is in accordance with TSAT and alerts all relevant Airport CDM Partners when no start up has been granted.
In case the start up approval is not granted at TSAT + tolerance, all relevant partners should be informed.
The flight will be re-sequenced.
Start up is requested by flight crew (voice or DCL) or at a locally defined time around TSAT if Milestone Process 13 is omitted.

milestones.name: Off-Block
rules: The process informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners of Actual Off-Block Time (AOBT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft has commenced push-back/taxi from parking position when it occurs.
The process checks if TTOT changes by more than the agreed tolerance and informs Network Operations.
TTOT is updated considering the EXOT.
AOBT always triggers an A-DPI message to Network Operations, or in the case of remote holding at a defined time prior to TTOT.
After a first A-DPI is sent this check shall be performed to check TTOT updates against the TTOT tolerance before Network Operations is informed, with a new A-DPI, of the updated TTOT.

milestones.name: Take Off
rules: FSA and MVT messages are sent.
The process informs all relevant Airport CDM Partners about the actual take off.
An airborne message is generated and the flight is removed from the departure sequence.
This process is triggered by Tower FDPS, A-SMGCS/Radar detection or ACARS.
